title: Yara and the Spire
premise: Ulyana Okafor has spent her life carving bones for the Guild of Impossible Things, listening to the dead whisper through her work while keeping her own name off every ledger. When a dying courier presses a map of Vessia—a country erased from all records forty years ago—into her hands, she becomes the last living key to a door that only opens for those who remember it. Hunted by the guild she serves and guided by the increasingly urgent voices of the dead, Ulyana must reconstruct the memory of a nation from bone-carvings, ledgers, and lies. At the spire where the last dragon-fire gutters out, she learns the truth: the guild itself erased Vessia to hoard its impossible things, and her own grandmother helped write it out of existence. Ulyana chooses truth over loyalty, speaks Vessia's name aloud at the door, and lets the dragon-fire die—freeing the dead and scattering the guild's hoard—before walking into a country that exists again because someone finally refused to forget it.
about_author: Ines Vasquez is a former archivist who spent six years cataloging the possessions of families displaced by border redrawings, an experience that haunts everything she writes. She lives in a coastal city with too many maps and a cat named after a country that no longer appears on any of them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the guildhouse at Grayharbor, Ulyana carves a dead woman's femur and hears her final secret: a name spoken twice, 'Vessia.' Establishes her gift, her careful invisibility within the guild, and her rule never to repeat what the dead say. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being a vessel for other people's truths while keeping none of her own.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Bone-Door
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses in the guildyard, pressing a folded map into Ulyana's hands before dying in her arms—whispering that she is 'the granddaughter of the one who wrote us out.' The guild's enforcers arrive asking questions. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility as Ulyana hides the map inside a half-carved bone, breaking her own rules for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with an interlude from Master Corvel's ledger entries. Ulyana investigates the guild's vaults under pretense of inventory, discovering objects tagged with a country name that appears in no atlas: Vessia. She realizes the guild trades in things stolen from erased places. Emotional beat: dawning horror that her employers are not merchants but thieves of existence itself.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Hand
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Searching her late grandmother's effects, Ulyana finds ledgers in a familiar hand—the same handwriting on the original decree that unmade Vessia. The dead woman from chapter one begins speaking to her through every bone she touches now, urgent and repeating. Emotional beat: grief curdling into betrayal; inheritance revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Fleeing Grayharbor before dawn, Ulyana follows the map into marshlands where roads appear only when she speaks fragments of remembered Vessian songs. A guild tracker shadows her. She meets Tam, a smuggler whose family were Vessian exiles who forgot why they mourn. Emotional beat: fragile hope—memory made literal, shaping the world underfoot.

chapters.title: Tam's Empty Village
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Tam POVs. They reach Tam's ancestral village: houses stand, fields grow wild, but no one remembers living there. The dead of Vessia crowd around Ulyana, begging to be named. The tracker attacks; Tam is wounded defending her. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty tested—Tam must choose between the comfortable forgetting and the painful truth Ulyana carries.

chapters.title: Corvel's Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Master Corvel catches up to them—not with violence but with an offer: return the map, take her grandmother's seat on the guild council, and live rich and safe. He reveals the guild erased Vessia because its 'impossible things' could unmake erasure anywhere, threatening every secret the guild keeps. Emotional beat: temptation and clarity; Ulyana sees that accepting means becoming her grandmother.

chapters.title: The Spire
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tam's POV, converging. They climb the Spire of Vessia as the last dragon-fire gutters in its brazier at the summit—the flame that burns on belief, nearly starved of rememberers. The dead press close, showing Ulyana the door at the spire's heart, which opens only for one who can speak the whole truth of what was done. Emotional beat: awe and dread; the climax approaches as the fire dims to an ember.

chapters.title: The Whole Truth
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax. Corvel arrives; Tam holds him off, wounded again. At the door, Ulyana speaks the full truth—including her grandmother's crime and her own years of willful silence—and names every dead Vessian she carries. The door opens; the dragon-fire flares once, magnificent, then gutters out forever as the dead pass through, freed. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release; truth costs everything and gives back more.

chapters.title: A Country With a Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tam's POV. Resolution. The guild's hoard scatters back to the places it was stolen from; Corvel, bound by his own ledgers, faces the guild's reckoning. Vessia flickers back onto maps and into memories. Ulyana carves her first bone with no voice inside it—her own—and signs her name in a new ledger. Emotional beat: quiet joy; inheritance reclaimed as something chosen rather than imposed.
